title: Natural comparison of strict derived inverse limit and the product cone
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume countable products in $\mathcal A$ are exact. Let $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ be the category of strict inverse sequences with levelwise exactness [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], and use the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a complex $X_\bullet$ of strict towers with transitions $t_n:X_{n+1}\to X_n$, put
$$\mathsf C(X_\bullet)=\operatorname{Cone}\left(1-s:\prod_{n\geq1}X_n\longrightarrow\prod_{n\geq1}X_n\right)[-1],\qquad s((x_n)_n)=(t_nx_{n+1})_n.$$
The products here are termwise products of complexes. This construction and its maps from strictly commuting squares descend to a functor $\mathsf C:D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))\to D(\mathcal A)$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$\rho_X:\mathsf C(X_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim X_\bullet,$$
where $R\lim$ is total derived inverse limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Its normalization is the following: if $q:X_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ is a K-injective tower resolution with injective terms [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], the canonical inclusion $\lim I_\bullet\to\mathsf C(I_\bullet)$, with zero component in the shifted product, is a quasi-isomorphism, and $\rho_X$ is the class of $\mathsf C(q)$ followed by the inverse of that inclusion. It commutes with each projection to $X_n$.
For a complex $P$ and strictly compatible chain maps $\gamma_n:P\to X_n$, the map $P\to\mathsf C(X_\bullet)$ with product component $(\gamma_n)_n$ and zero shifted-product component corresponds under $\rho_X$ to the canonical derived map $P\to R\lim X_\bullet$ induced by the strict augmentation. This comparison and this assertion are independent of the chosen resolution.
